R5D-bear-drive-0002.name: By Gaspard Creek
R5D-bear-drive-0002.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).
R5D-bear-drive-0002.parkWhat: pull off on Gaspard Creek FSR (gravel road)

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2017 (9 years old), right here: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
Burn from 2017 (fire C50647), right here: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
SW facing slope, 13 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Gaspard Creek 60 m SW: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from Soda Creek, about 116 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate). Via Soda Creek Townsite Rd, Williams Lake Cut-Off Rd, Soda Creek Rd, MacKenzie Ave N.
Park: 51.59502, -122.71457, pull off on Gaspard Creek FSR (gravel road). Map links below.
Walk: 280 m W, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 0 m, about 6 min at 3 km/h.

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 5-3, Region 5. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-07, closures 2026-10-16.
R5D-bear-drive-0002.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 5-3: about 480 hunter days a year for black bear (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.13 days per square km, middle third of BC MUs; access: average access. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).

tags.label: Good for 2
tags.why: Cover edge here (cutblock or burn): one hunter sits at a crossing or glasses, the other walks the edge slowly with the wind at their back toward the stander. Agree zones of fire, a meeting point and a time at the truck (Tip, lesson: Hunting with a partner). Pushes are on foot only (99%, synopsis page 11, item 25).

tags.label: Good solo
tags.why: Short pack out: 0.3 km and about 0 m of climb from the parking (Tip). Cell coverage is not in the data: leave a trip plan and carry SOS or a satellite messenger (lesson: Bush safety).

evidence.t: No official deer winter range within 500 m, so the top score here is 8 of 11. This score leans on cutblocks, burns, habitat zone and aspect.
Cutblock harvested 2017 (9 years old), right here.
Burn from 2017 (fire C50647, 239,340 ha), 880 m NW.
Habitat zone Interior Douglas fir (IDFdk4): low winter and fall range.
Private fields 1.8 km S: deer feed on field edges (fields are private).
